are dissolved in 250 mL of water.
(A) glucose (180 g mol-^1)
(B) sodium carbonate (106 g mol-^1)
(C) sodium hydroxide (40 g mol-^1)

Increasing order of molarity means increasing order of 1/M, which is decreasing order of M: M(glucose)=180 (lowest molarity), M(Na2CO3)=106, M(CH3COOH)=60, M(NaOH)=40 (highest molarity). Wait, let's check values: 180 > 106 > 60 > 40. So Molarity is: Glucose < Na2CO3 < Acetic acid < NaOH? For same w, Molarity is inversely proportional to M. Thus Molarity order (increasing): M is largest to smallest: Glucose (180) -> lowest molarity (A). Next largest M is Na2CO3 (106) -> second lowest. Wait! Let's check Option B: (A), (D), (C), (B) corresponds to Glucose (180), Acetic acid (60), NaOH (40), Sodium carbonate (106) - wait, molar mass of Na2CO3 is 106, which is smaller than 180 but larger than 60.
